commands.name: deep-research

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. import logging

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl

from flag_gems.utils import pointwise_dynamic

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@pointwise_dynamic(is_tensor=[True, True], promotion_methods=[(0, 1, "DEFAULT")])
@triton.jit
def logaddexp2_func(x, y):
    # log2(2**x + 2**y) = m + log2(1 + 2**(-|x - y|)), m = max(x, y)
    x_f32 = x.to(tl.float32)
    y_f32 = y.to(tl.float32)
    m = tl.maximum(x_f32, y_f32)
    delta = x_f32 - y_f32
    res = m + tl.log2(1.0 + tl.exp2(-tl.abs(delta)))
    # `delta` is NaN when x and y are equal infinities (inf - inf); the result
    # is then m, e.g. logaddexp2(inf, inf) = inf, logaddexp2(-inf, -inf) = -inf.
    res = tl.where(delta != delta, m, res)
    # Genuine NaN inputs must still propagate NaN.
    is_nan = (x_f32 != x_f32) | (y_f32 != y_f32)
    return tl.where(is_nan, float("nan"), res)


@triton.jit
def _logaddexp2_flat_kernel(
    x_ptr,
    y_ptr,
    out_ptr,
    n,
    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
    LOOPS: tl.constexpr,
    EVEN: tl.constexpr,
    OUT_F32: tl.constexpr,
):
    # One program handles LOOPS consecutive tiles of BLOCK elements.  The grid
    # is bounded, so every program walks its tiles with a grid stride until the
    # whole flat range is covered; there is no trailing remainder either way
    # because `n` is always an exact multiple of BLOCK * LOOPS here.
    span = BLOCK * LOOPS
    stride = tl.num_programs(0) * span
    start = tl.program_id(0) * span
    arange = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
    for base in range(start, n, stride):
        for i in range(LOOPS):
            offs = base + i * BLOCK + arange
            if EVEN:
                xv = tl.load(x_ptr + offs)
                yv = tl.load(y_ptr + offs)
            else:
                mask = offs < n
                xv = tl.load(x_ptr + offs, mask=mask, other=0.0)
                yv = tl.load(y_ptr + offs, mask=mask, other=0.0)
            # `max` stays in the input dtype; only the difference and the
            # correction term are promoted to FP32.
            m = tl.maximum(xv, yv)
            diff = xv.to(tl.float32) - yv.to(tl.float32)
            t = tl.abs(diff)
            # inf - inf produces a NaN difference for equal infinities: the
            # result is then m, so clamp the NaN to 0 and cap the magnitude at
            # 200 (2**-200 underflows in FP32, the correction collapses to 0).
            t = tl.where(t != t, 0.0, t)
            t = tl.minimum(t, 200.0)
            # log2(1 + 2**-t) = ln(1 + exp2(-t)) * log2(e); the `+1` stays
            # inside the log so there is no cancellation for small t.
            corr = tl.log(1.0 + tl.exp2(-t)) * 1.4426950408889634
            r = m.to(tl.float32) + corr
            # Genuine NaN inputs must still propagate NaN.
            is_nan = (xv != xv) | (yv != yv)
            r = tl.where(is_nan, float("nan"), r)
            if OUT_F32:
                rv = r
            else:
                rv = r.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty)
            if EVEN:
                tl.store(out_ptr + offs, rv)
            else:
                tl.store(out_ptr + offs, rv, mask=mask)


def _can_fast_path(x, y, out):
    if not isinstance(x, torch.Tensor) or not isinstance(y, torch.Tensor):
        return False
    if x.device != y.device or x.dtype != y.dtype:
        return False
    if out.device != x.device or out.dtype != x.dtype:
        return False
    if not x.is_contiguous() or not y.is_contiguous() or not out.is_contiguous():
        return False
    if x.shape != y.shape or x.shape != out.shape:
        return False
    if x.numel() == 0:
        return False
    if x.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32):
        return False
    return True


def _flat_config(numel, itemsize):
    # tile sizes follow the previously validated split for this operator:
    # a 8192-element tile for half precision, 4096 for FP32, and 4096 for the
    # very large tensors where UB pressure matters more than reuse.
    if itemsize == 4:
        block, target = 4096, 1
    else:
        block, target = 8192, 2
    loops = 1
    total = block
    # Keep at least 4x the number of physical AIV cores so that the grid can
    # still saturate the device for small and medium tensors.
    max_programs = max(4096, numel // (block * 4))
    while total * 2 <= numel and total < max_programs * block:
        total *= 2
        loops *= 2
    return block, loops


def _launch_flat(x, y, out, block, loops):
    n = out.numel()
    span = block * loops
    grid = (min(triton.cdiv(n, span), 65535),)
    even = (n % span) == 0
    out_f32 = out.dtype == torch.float32
    _logaddexp2_flat_kernel[grid](
        x, y, out, n, BLOCK=block, LOOPS=loops, EVEN=even, OUT_F32=out_f32
    )


def logaddexp2(self, other):
    logger.debug("GEMS LOGADDEXP2")
    if isinstance(self, torch.Tensor) and isinstance(other, torch.Tensor):
        try:
            promoted = torch.promote_types(self.dtype, other.dtype)
        except TypeError:
            promoted = None
        if promoted is not None and promoted in (
            torch.float16,
            torch.bfloat16,
            torch.float32,
        ):
            # Reproduce the generic path's type promotion without going
            # through it, so the fast path sees exactly the same operands.
            xc = self if self.dtype == promoted else self.to(promoted)
            yc = other if other.dtype == promoted else other.to(promoted)
            if xc.dtype == yc.dtype and xc.numel() == yc.numel():
                out = torch.empty_like(xc)
                if _can_fast_path(xc, yc, out):
                    block, loops = _flat_config(out.numel(), out.element_size())
                    _launch_flat(xc, yc, out, block, loops)
                    return out
    return logaddexp2_func(self, other)


def logaddexp2_out(self, other, out):
    logger.debug("GEMS LOGADDEXP2_OUT")
    if isinstance(self, torch.Tensor) and isinstance(other, torch.Tensor):
        try:
            promoted = torch.promote_types(self.dtype, other.dtype)
        except TypeError:
            promoted = None
        if promoted is not None and out.dtype == promoted and out.element_size() in (
            2,
            4,
        ):
            xc = self if self.dtype == promoted else self.to(promoted)
            yc = other if other.dtype == promoted else other.to(promoted)
            if xc.dtype == yc.dtype and xc.numel() == yc.numel():
                if _can_fast_path(xc, yc, out):
                    block, loops = _flat_config(out.numel(), out.element_size())
                    _launch_flat(xc, yc, out, block, loops)
                    return out
    logaddexp2_func(self, other, out0=out)
    return out

关键几何设计（针对慢 case 而不是只改注释）：
1) 超大 shape（1073741824 元素，fp16/bf16/fp32 各 2 个 case，现 69~71 ms、0.10~0.22×）：网格上界 `min(cdiv(n, BLOCK*LOOPS), 65535)`，越界部分由 kernel 里的运行时 `for base in range(start, n, stride)` 做 grid-stride 覆盖，保证 n 全部被处理；`_flat_config` 在大 n 时 block=8192(fp16/bf16)/4096(fp32)、loops 按 2 的幂增长到 `4*numel/block` 上限，使每个 program 连续处理多个 tile、program 数由上万个降到千级，减少标量与调度开销（该 case 真机 aiv_scalar_ratio=0.22、mte2=0.356、mte3=0.174，说明确实存在非 vector 的固定开销）。

}

            # log2(1 + 2**-t) = ln(1 + exp2(-t)) * log2(e); the `+1` stays
            # inside the log so there is no cancellation for small t.
            corr = tl.log(1.0 + tl.exp2(-t)) * 1.4426950408889634
            r = m.to(tl.float32) + corr
            # Genuine NaN inputs must still propagate NaN.
            is_nan = (xv != xv) | (yv != yv)
            r = tl.where(is_nan, float("nan"), r)
            if OUT_F32:
                rv = r
            else:
                rv = r.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty)
            if EVEN:
                tl.store(out_ptr + offs, rv)
            else:
                tl.store(out_ptr + offs, rv, mask=mask)


def _can_fast_path(x, y, out):
    if not isinstance(x, torch.Tensor) or not isinstance(y, torch.Tensor):
        return False
    if x.device != y.device or x.dtype != y.dtype:
        return False
    if out.device != x.device or out.dtype != x.dtype:
        return False
    if not x.is_contiguous() or not y.is_contiguous() or not out.is_contiguous():
        return False
    if x.shape != y.shape or x.shape != out.shape:
        return False
    if x.numel() == 0:
        return False
    if x.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32):
        return False
    return True


def _flat_config(numel, itemsize):
    # tile sizes follow the previously validated split for this operator:
    # a 8192-element tile for half precision, 4096 for FP32, and 4096 for the
    # very large tensors where UB pressure matters more than reuse.
    if itemsize == 4:
        block, target = 4096, 1
    else:
        block, target = 8192, 2
    loops = 1
    total = block
    # Keep at least 4x the number of physical AIV cores so that the grid can
    # still saturate the device for small and medium tensors.
    max_programs = max(4096, numel // (block * 4))
    while total * 2 <= numel and total < max_programs * block:
        total *= 2
        loops *= 2
    return block, loops


def _launch_flat(x, y, out, block, loops):
    n = out.numel()
    span = block * loops
    grid = (min(triton.cdiv(n, span), 65535),)
    even = (n % span) == 0
    out_f32 = out.dtype == torch.float32
    _logaddexp2_flat_kernel[grid](
        x, y, out, n, BLOCK=block, LOOPS=loops, EVEN=even, OUT_F32=out_f32
    )


def logaddexp2(self, other):
    logger.debug("GEMS LOGADDEXP2")
    if isinstance(self, torch.Tensor) and isinstance(other, torch.Tensor):
        try:
            promoted = torch.promote_types(self.dtype, other.dtype)
        except TypeError:
            promoted = None
        if promoted is not None and promoted in (
            torch.float16,
            torch.bfloat16,
            torch.float32,
        ):
            # Reproduce the generic path's type promotion without going
            # through it, so the fast path sees exactly the same operands.
            xc = self if self.dtype == promoted else self.to(promoted)
            yc = other if other.dtype == promoted else other.to(promoted)
            if xc.dtype == yc.dtype and xc.numel() == yc.numel():
                out = torch.empty_like(xc)
                if _can_fast_path(xc, yc, out):
                    block, loops = _flat_config(out.numel(), out.element_size())
                    _launch_flat(xc, yc, out, block, loops)
                    return out
    return logaddexp2_func(self, other)


def logaddexp2_out(self, other, out):
    logger.debug("GEMS LOGADDEXP2_OUT")
    if isinstance(self, torch.Tensor) and isinstance(other, torch.Tensor):
        try:
            promoted = torch.promote_types(self.dtype, other.dtype)
        except TypeError:
            promoted = None
        if promoted is not None and out.dtype == promoted and out.element_size() in (
            2,
            4,
        ):
            xc = self if self.dtype == promoted else self.to(promoted)
            yc = other if other.dtype == promoted else other.to(promoted)
            if xc.dtype == yc.dtype and xc.numel() == yc.numel():
                if _can_fast_path(xc, yc, out):
                    block, loops = _flat_config(out.numel(), out.element_size())
                    _launch_flat(xc, yc, out, block, loops)
                    return out
    logaddexp2_func(self, other, out0=out)
    return out
